name: lynxdi-pdf-studio
description: PDFs as code — built for coding agents. 100 composable PDF operations, one workflow language: tell a coding agent what you want; it authors an OpenPDF Workflow (OPW) file that a deterministic engine renders locally. pdf-lib bundled; PyMuPDF/pikepdf/qpdf optional.

chatInstructions.description: How to edit PDFs in a PDF Studio workspace: author an OpenPDF Workflow (.opw.yaml) and use the pdf-studio MCP tools.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No OpenPDF Workflow found.
Create a starter project (workflow.opw.yaml + sample inputs) to get started.
[Initialize PDF Studio Project](command:pdfStudio.initProject)
[New Workflow](command:pdfStudio.newWorkflow)
Or download runnable example projects to learn from:
[Get Example Projects](command:pdfStudio.downloadExamples)

pdfStudio.pythonPath.description: Python executable used to probe and run the optional PyMuPDF/pikepdf/OCR backend. Empty = python3/python on PATH. Machine-scoped: cannot be set by a workspace (a workspace must not choose which interpreter runs).

pdfStudio.paddlePythonPath.markdownDescription: Python executable of a SEPARATE venv that has PaddleOCR-VL installed (the `extract_markdown` / `pdf_to_markdown` `engine: paddleocr-vl`). Kept apart from `#pdfStudio.pythonPath#` because the PaddlePaddle stack conflicts with the PyMuPDF/marker pins. Empty = use the extension-managed venv created by **PDF Studio: Set up PaddleOCR-VL** (click the PaddleOCR-VL row in the Dependencies view). Machine-scoped.

pdfStudio.vlmEndpoint.markdownDescription: OpenAI-compatible base URL (ending in `/v1`) of the vision-language model server used by `extract_receipt` — e.g. `http://localhost:11434/v1` (Ollama) or `http://gpu:8801/v1` (vLLM). Set automatically by **PDF Studio: Set up Receipt OCR (Qwen3-VL)**. Empty = fall back to the `$PDFSTUDIO_VLM_ENDPOINT` environment variable. Machine-scoped.

pdfStudio.vlmModel.markdownDescription: Model name `extract_receipt` requests from the VLM server (e.g. `qwen2.5vl:3b`, or a fine-tuned `qwen3-vl-8b-receipts`). Empty = fall back to `$PDFSTUDIO_VLM_MODEL`. Machine-scoped.

pdfStudio.autoRenderOnSave.description: Re-render a workflow's output automatically whenever its .opw.yaml is saved.

pdfStudio.autoValidateOnSave.description: Validate a workflow and surface diagnostics in the Problems panel whenever its .opw.yaml is saved.

pdfStudio.telemetry.enabled.markdownDescription: **Off by default.** Turn on to send anonymous, non-identifying usage events (which features/operations are used) to help prioritize development — no file paths, contents, names, or personal data, ever. Also requires VS Code's global telemetry (`#telemetry.telemetryLevel#`). This is a local-first tool: it collects nothing unless you opt in here.

pdfStudio.telemetry.debug.markdownDescription: Log every telemetry event and its HTTP status to the **PDF Studio: Telemetry** output channel, to confirm what is (and isn't) sent.

pdfStudio.allowRemoteRender.markdownDescription: Allow operations with a `remote` (SSH) or `endpoint` (HTTP) parameter to offload rendering to a remote GPU box (e.g. `extract_markdown` with `engine: marker`). **This uploads your document bytes to the host/URL you specify** — Marker runs there on the GPU and the Markdown is downloaded — minutes on a 4090 vs hours on a CPU. SSH needs key-based auth + `scp` on PATH (`user@host`, no shell metacharacters); the HTTP `endpoint` may be any `http(s)://` URL you control (chunked + resumable for large files). **Off by default** because it sends data to another machine; machine-scoped so a workspace cannot enable it. This is also the gate for `extract_receipt`, which sends PAGE IMAGES to a vision-language model server — document-byte egress is governed here, not by `#pdfStudio.allowAiRequests#`.

pdfStudio.allowAiRequests.markdownDescription: Allow the **text** AI operations (`summarize`, `translate`, `semantic_search`, and `detect: ai`) to send the document's extracted TEXT to a language model. **By default this uses a LOCAL model via Ollama** (`OLLAMA_HOST`, default `http://localhost:11434`) so nothing leaves your machine; set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to use Claude (cloud), or point `PDFSTUDIO_LLM_ENDPOINT`/`PDFSTUDIO_EMBED_ENDPOINT` at a free NVIDIA cloud model with `NVIDIA_API_KEY` (see docs/python-setup.md). `PDFSTUDIO_LLM_MODEL` picks the model. **Off by default** because these ops send document content to a model; machine-scoped so a workspace cannot enable it. When off, an AI op fails with a clear message rather than contacting any model. **This setting does not cover ops that upload document BYTES or PAGE IMAGES to a host you name** — `extract_markdown`/`pdf_to_markdown` with `remote`/`endpoint` (Marker) and `extract_receipt` (a vision-language model) are gated by `#pdfStudio.allowRemoteRender#` instead, even though `extract_receipt` is listed under Document intelligence (AI).

pdfStudio.scaffoldEmptyWorkspace.description: When PDF Studio activates in an empty folder, seed a sample OPW project so there is something to render immediately.

pdfStudio.generateAgentMap.description: When you run 'Initialize Project', also write CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / GEMINI.md so a coding agent knows how to edit OPW workflows here. These files are NEVER created automatically on activation — only on an explicit Initialize Project / Generate Agent Map action. Set false to skip them even on init.

pdfStudio.examplesUrl.markdownDescription: Base URL the **Get Example Projects** action downloads runnable example bundles from (must serve `manifest.json` + one `.zip` per example). Empty = the built-in Lynx CDN default. Must be `https://` (or `http://localhost` for local development — point it at `http://localhost:8080/examples/`, `npm run site:serve`). Machine-scoped: a workspace cannot redirect example downloads.

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with PDF Studio
walkthroughs.description: Render a PDF from a YAML workflow, fill a real government form from your own records, and turn a Word document into a fillable PDF — then read the answers back as a spreadsheet.

steps.title: Render a PDF from a workflow
steps.description:
Create a starter project, then hit Render. The YAML is the source of truth; the PDF is the build artifact.
[Initialize Project](command:pdfStudio.initProject)
Then: [Render Workflow](command:pdfStudio.runWorkflow) and [Open Preview](command:pdfStudio.openPreview)

media.altText: A workflow.opw.yaml rendering to a PDF

steps.title: Fill a real form (W-9, 1040, I-9…)
steps.description:
12 government forms ship already mapped. Put your details in a local, gitignored people.yaml — or point at a CSV — and fill any of them.
[Create People File](command:pdfStudio.initPeople)
Browse the forms in the PDF Fill sidebar.

media.altText: Filling an IRS W-9 from a people.yaml record

steps.title: Turn a Word doc into a fillable PDF
steps.description:
Type [[check]] and [[text]] in Word where fields belong; create_form makes them real form fields. Then extract_form reads the filled copies back into a CSV.
[Browse the operations](command:pdfStudio.showOpReference)

media.altText: A Word template becoming a fillable PDF, then a CSV

steps.title: Light up the optional dependencies
steps.description:
The bundled engine needs nothing installed. OCR, redaction, forms and Office conversion light up when their dependency is present — the Dependencies view shows what you have and what each one unlocks.
[Check Dependencies](command:pdfStudio.checkDependencies)

scripts.release: npm run package && npm run install-local
